trial_name.text: Two Phase 3 aortoiliac MRA studies, MS-325-12 and MS-325-13 (combined/re-read for approval)

citations.quote: The NDA21711 resubmission is dedicated to results from a Re-Read of image data from two previously submitted studies: MS-325-12 and MS-325-13.
Safety and efficacy of VASOVIST were assessed in two multi-center, open-label, Phase 3 clinical trials.
The NDA21711 resubmission is dedicated to results from a Re-Read of image data from two previously submitted studies: MS-325-12 and MS-325-13.
Safety and efficacy of VASOVIST were assessed in two multi-center, open-label, Phase 3 clinical trials.

design.text: Two multi-center, open-label, single-arm (blinded-read) Phase 3 trials; patients underwent MRA with and without VASOVIST and catheter-based X-ray arteriography as the reference standard

citations.quote: Both studies were open label, single arm studies.

In both trials, patients with known or suspected peripheral vascular disease underwent MRA with and without VASOVIST as well as catheter-based X-ray arteriography. Diagnostic efficacy was based upon comparisons of sensitivity and specificity between MRA with and without VASOVIST, with X-ray arteriography as the reference standard.

population.text: Adults with known or suspected peripheral vascular disease evaluated for aortoiliac occlusive disease; median age 67 years (range 29 to 87), 83% white, 68% male

citations.quote: In these 424 patients, the median age was 67 years with a range of 29 to 87 years; 58% of the patients were over 65 years of age; 83% were white and 68% were male.

endpoint.text: Superiority in sensitivity and non-inferiority in specificity of VASOVIST-MRA versus non-contrast MRA at the vessel-segment level for detecting occlusive disease (>=50% stenosis)

citations.quote: The primary efficacy analyses were designed to demonstrate superiority in sensitivity and non-inferiority in specificity of VASOVIST-MRA as compared to non-contrast MRA at the vessel-segment level.

Out of 493 patients enrolled in these two trials, 424 were included in the comparison of the diagnostic efficacy of VASOVIST-MRA to that of non-contrast MRA in detection/exclusion of occlusive vascular disease (\ge 50\% stenosis) in 7 vessel-segments in the aortoiliac region.

n.text: 493 patients enrolled across the two trials; 424 included in the diagnostic efficacy comparison

citations.quote: Out of 493 patients enrolled in these two trials, 424 were included in the comparison of the diagnostic efficacy of VASOVIST-MRA to that of non-contrast MRA in detection/exclusion of occlusive vascular disease (\ge 50\% stenosis) in 7 vessel-segments in the aortoiliac region.

result.text: Superiority in sensitivity and non-inferiority in specificity demonstrated by all three readers; sensitivity differences VASOVIST-MRA vs non-contrast: 20% (95% CI 15%, 25%), 12% (7%, 17%), 15% (9%, 21%)

citations.quote: Superiority in sensitivity and non-inferiority in specificity was demonstrated for VASOVIST-MRA by all three blinded readers.

indication.text: Gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated for use in magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) to evaluate aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) in adults with known or suspected peripheral vascular disease

citations.quote: VASOVIST Injection is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated for use as a contrast agent in magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) to evaluate aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) in adults with known or suspected peripheral vascular disease.

target_moa.text: Following IV injection, gadofosveset binds reversibly to endogenous serum albumin, giving a longer vascular residence time and increasing magnetic resonance relaxivity, which shortens the T1 relaxation time of water protons and increases blood signal intensity (brightness)

citations.quote: Following intravenous injection, gadofosveset binds reversibly to endogenous serum albumin resulting in longer vascular residence time than non-protein binding contrast agents.

The binding to serum albumin also increases the magnetic resonance relaxivity of gadofosveset and decreases the relaxation time (T_1) of water protons resulting in an increase in signal intensity (brightness) of blood.

modality.text: Small molecule gadolinium-based contrast agent (gadolinium GdDTPA chelate with a diphenylcyclohexylphosphate group), a radiopharmaceutical/imaging agent

citations.quote: VASOVIST (gadofosveset trisodium) Injection is a sterile, nonpyrogenic, formulation of a stable gadolinium diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (GdDTPA) chelate derivative with a diphenylcyclohexylphosphate group.

key_safety.text: Most common (>2%) adverse reactions: pruritus (5%), headache (4%), nausea (4%), vasodilatation (3%) and paresthesia (3%); anaphylaxis/anaphylactoid reactions were the most common serious reactions (2 of 1676 subjects)

citations.quote: The most common (> 2%) adverse reactions are pruritus, headache, nausea, vasodilatation and paresthesia (6.1, 6.2).

detail.text: Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis (NSF): gadolinium-based contrast agents increase the risk for NSF in patients with acute or chronic severe renal insufficiency (GFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2) or acute renal insufficiency of any severity due to hepato-renal syndrome or in the perioperative liver transplantation period

citations.quote: ## WARNING: NEPHROGENIC SYSTEMIC FIBROSIS (NSF)

- acute or chronic severe renal insufficiency (glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73m^2), or
- acute renal insufficiency of any severity due to the hepato-renal syndrome or in the perioperative liver transplantation period.

vote.text: Not presented to an Advisory Committee because the product is a member of the GBCA class and did not present unique safety concerns

citations.quote: This application was not presented to an Advisory Committee because the product is a member of the class of GBCA and did not present unique safety concerns nor difficulty in interpretation of the data from the image reread.

detail.text: Not first cycle; originally submitted October 2004, received an approvable letter, and FDA again issued an approvable letter in November 2005; the June 30, 2008 submission constituted a complete response to the November 21, 2005 action letter (third cycle)

citations.quote: The application was originally submitted in October, 2004. That review cycle concluded with the issuance of an "approvable" letter.
The June 30, 2008, submission constituted a complete response to our November 21, 2005, action letter.
Date of Submission	July 1, 2008 (third cycle)

requirement.text: A clinical trial to collect clinical data sufficient to assess the magnitude of risk for the development of NSF with the product among patients with moderate (GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2) to severe renal insufficiency (required under section 505(o)(3))

citations.quote: - A clinical trial to collect clinical data sufficient to assess the magnitude of risk for the development of NSF with your product among patients with moderate (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2) to severe renal insufficiency.
Therefore, based on appropriate scientific data, FDA has determined that you are required, pursuant to section 505(o)(3) of the FDCA, to conduct the following clinical trial:

date.text: November 21, 2005 action letter (approvable); earlier approvable letter after October 2004 submission

citations.quote: The June 30, 2008, submission constituted a complete response to our November 21, 2005, action letter.
The application was originally submitted in October, 2004. That review cycle concluded with the issuance of an "approvable" letter.

basis.text: Lack of persuasive diagnostic efficacy data; FDA noted the data did not provide conclusive evidence that Vasovist added value to MRA performed without Vasovist

citations.quote: FDA issued an approvable letter in November, 2005, again citing the lack of persuasive diagnostic efficacy data.

summary.text: New molecular entity GBCA approved under section 505(b) following a complicated multi-cycle regulatory history (two prior approvable letters, 2004 and November 2005) that was resolved by a re-read of the two aortoiliac studies; approved as the first FDA-approved agent for MRA, with a 505(o) post-marketing NSF clinical trial requirement and a boxed warning for NSF

citations.quote: This New Drug Application (NDA) was submitted for gadofosveset trisodium injection (Vasovist), a new molecular entity within the class of products generally referred to as "gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs)."
This application has a complicated regulatory history.
Hence, Vasovist will be the first FDA-approved agent for magnetic resonance angiography (MRA).
